breast cancer patients treated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) who achieve a pathological complete response (pCR) have a significantly better survival than non-pCR patients.

The results of the study show that the risk of local recurrence after breast-conservation therapy is higher for patients who are diagnosed with HER-2-positive, ER-positive and/or PR-negative tumors, compared to patients with HER-2-negative, ER-positive and PR-positive tumors.
the risk of local and distant recurrence was higher for patients with luminal B breast cancer than with luminal A breast cancer after breast-conserving surgery with radiotherapy.

the results are inconclusive.

the evidence is sufficient to conclude that breast-conserving therapy is effective in reducing the risk of local recurrence compared with mastectomy in women with stage I and stage II breast cancer, and in reducing the risk for distant recurrence compared with total mastectomy in women who have undergone breast-conserving therapy.

there is no evidence that breast cancer patients who are treated with radiation therapy to the chest wall and regional lymph nodes after breast conserving surgery have an increased risk of second primary malignancies in the chest wall.

the HER-2 status of the primary tumour is an essential predictor of the chance of recurrence after BCT.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the risk of recurrence after breast-conservation therapy (BCT) is associated with breast cancer subtypes approximated by estrogen-receptor (ER), progesterone-receptor (PR), and HER-2 status.
the HER2 subtype of breast cancer has a very high recurrence risk.
the use of a breast cancer subtype-specific treatment approach is associated with improved outcomes.
